messages:
samir: FYI escalated from @support — Acme reports sharp p99 jump on text-generation endpoint in us-west2 :rotating_light:
support-bot: New escalation #SEV3 -> posted customer logs + request IDs 98f3a2..98f3d0
elaine: looking — can you paste an example request id and time window?
support-bot: request ids: 98f3a2, 98f3a9, 98f3d0. spike started ~2025-11-03T14:02:00Z, p99 ~2.4s (baseline ~0.9s). small prompts workload.
devon: I pulled traces — lots of requests hitting continuous-batcher path with hold_window ~12ms and coalesce enabled. KV-cache hits steady. tail latency aligns with batching hold expirations.
anya: is this the new grace-window change we rolled last night? I thought we reduced hold time to 8ms for lower avg latency.
devon: rollout added adaptive grace that increases hold when throughput low; looks like for tiny prompts it ends up coalescing into tiny microbatches then waiting longer (~12ms) to reach min batch size -> p99 spike.
maria: query I ran: ```sql
SELECT
  percentile(lat_ms, 95) as p95,
  percentile(lat_ms, 99) as p99,
  count(*)
FROM request_metrics
WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND region='us-west2' AND ts BETWEEN '2025-11-03T13:50' AND '2025-11-03T14:10';
```
results: p95 0.92s p99 2.38s, spike coincides with about 30% drop in concurrent requests for that tenant.
samir: customer is on hosted API with dedicated routing? any auth/billing anomalies? they mentioned retries earlier.
elaine: no auth/billing errors. 429s unchanged. This is purely batching hold dynamics.
anya: quick mitigation idea: temporarily disable adaptive_grace for affected pool (force GRACE_WINDOW_MS=4) or enable fastpath for tiny payloads to bypass coalesce. Which is lower risk?
devon: fastpath needs a small binary flag but safe to toggle — it forces immediate dispatch for payloads < 128 bytes. I'd prefer fastpath short-term.
maria: I can run a canary toggle on 10% of tokens in us-west2. telemetry query ready.
samir: do it. @deploy-bot schedule canary, record rollback window.
deploy-bot: canary toggle scheduled: feature=coalesce_fastpath target=10% region=us-west2 starts=2025-11-03T14:30:00Z ends=2025-11-03T15:00:00Z :white_check_mark:
elaine: also roll back adaptive grace change from last night's deploy in parallel? that's riskier. maybe only if canary doesn't help.
devon: agree. I'll prepare a hotfix branch to pin GRACE_WINDOW_MS=4ms for the affected pool if toggle fails. Repro steps for local: 
```
# replay a tiny-prompts trace
python tools/replay.py --requests requests_small.json --batcher=continuous --grace=12
# expect: p99 > 2s
python tools/replay.py --requests requests_small.json --batcher=continuous --grace=4
# expect: p99 ~0.9s
```
anya: please attach the small requests trace file to the ticket. I'll update support with mitigation ETA and ask customer to avoid bursty probes while we canary.
support-bot: customer notified: "Our engineers are canarying a config change in us-west2 starting in 30m; we'll update in 30m or sooner."
maria: canary running now (10% traffic) — initial telemetry shows p99 for the canary cohort down to 0.95s while control remains 2.3s.
samir: nice. escalate to 50% if stable for 5m, otherwise rollback.
deploy-bot: canary scaled to 50% at 2025-11-03T14:36:00Z :rocket:
elaine: 50% looks good; let's plan full rollout and then follow with a careful revert of the adaptive-grace change in the next release to avoid recurrence.
devon: filed PR to add regression test in e2e that covers tiny prompt patterns and adaptive grace behavior.
anya: closing loop with customer: give them summary + invite to join post-mortem meeting.
samir: great work. added postmortem stub: /playbooks/postmortems/4891122334-coalesce-window-postmortem.md
support-bot: thread closed by samir at 2025-11-03T14:46:40Z :white_check_mark:
